about: Homer's Back Fat is a two-panel Simpsons scene in the couple's bedroom. In the top panel Homer stands in his briefs with hands on hips, suddenly slim, wearing a smug half-lidded grin while Marge looks on. In the bottom panel he turns around and the trick is revealed: all the excess skin and fat has been gathered behind him and pinned in place with clips, bulging in a lumpy mass from his back up to the folds clipped behind his head. The meme compares a polished front to the ugly mess holding it together behind the scenes.
origin: The scene is from The Simpsons episode "Husbands and Knives," first aired in November 2007, in which Homer turns to cosmetic surgery to keep up with Marge.
usage:
The top box sits on the slim, confident panel and names the thing that looks great from the front: a product, a website, a codebase demo, a tidy room. The bottom box sits on the reveal and names what is actually holding it together: hacks, debt, duct tape, a closet stuffed with junk.

It lands when the hidden mess is relatable and specific. Engineering, renovation, social media versus real life and suspiciously cheap budgets are all strong targets.
